**Thesis in one paragraph.** NVS is a pure-play innovative-medicines company that has just absorbed the largest patent expiry in its history (Entresto, Promacta, Tasigna — US generics 2025–2026) while simultaneously funding an $11–12B acquisition (Avidity, closed Feb-2026) that drove net debt from $21.9B to $39.4B. Management's mid-term targets (5% sales CAGR 2024–2029, ~40% core margin) are consistent with a business whose growth brands (Kisqali +55%, Pluvicto +70%, Kesimpta +26%, Scemblix +79% in Q1-2026) offset generic erosion. The valuation hinges on two variables the data pack leaves open: the **true cost of equity** (the vendor's 0.494 beta is far below any reasonable large-cap-pharma systematic risk estimate, and the pack explicitly refuses to stand behind it) and the **FCF definition** (pack capex $1.548B vs vendor $3.9B — a 2.5× gap that changes FCF by 15%). I take the conservative FCF definition and present the full cost-of-capital sensitivity rather than picking one beta silently.

## SECTION 1 — VALUATION ENGINE & FRAMEWORK

### 1.1 Selection: Why a 10-year explicit DCF with declining-then-stabilizing revenue path

The company's reported economics do not fit a single-period multiple: FY2026 is a **transition year** (low-single-digit sales growth, low-single-digit core-OI decline, Avidity integration costs), FY2027–2029 is the **mid-term acceleration phase** (company-targeted +5% CAGR), and FY2030–2034 is the **next patent-cliff absorption phase** (Kisqali, Cosentyx, Kesimpta LOEs fall in the early 2030s). A trailing multiple on FY2025 or FY2026 would mechanically undervalue the recovery; a Gordon growth model would require assuming a perpetual growth rate that cannot be sourced for the LOE window. The DCF framework is the only method that can make the timing explicit.

### 1.2 Identity and fiscal month
- Fiscal year = calendar year (Dec-2025 for FY2025). Dec-2025 is used as valuation date base-year; T0 price is as of 2026-08-24.

### 1.3 The cash-flow definition decision
FCF for valuation = **OCF − (PP&E capex + capitalized software)**.

| Component | FY2025 value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| OCF (filed) | $19.144B | Pack §5 |
| PP&E capex | $1.548B | Pack §5 (filed) |
| Capitalized software (inferred) | ~$2.35B | [Arithmetic] Vendor capex $3.900B − pack capex $1.548B; vendor definition = total capex. The pack flags its own number as excluding capitalised software. |
| **Adjusted FCF FY2025** | **~$15.24B (27.9% of revenue)** | This is the valuation base |

Pack FCF ($17.596B) is NOT used as the base — it is the numerator of a conversion that omits software spend. The vendor's stock-compensation scalar ($1.096B) is a real expense that OCF already nets out; no further deduction is needed beyond what OCF already reflects.

### 1.4 The 2026 one-time charge
**$0.3B** deduction from FY2026 FCF for Avidity-related integration/one-time costs (the Feb-2026 close was followed by pipeline-combination costs; the company does not break out the quantum — **$0.3B is my [Assumption], sized conservatively at ~2% of 2026 FCF**). This is a modest item; it does not move the valuation by more than $0.20/share.

## SECTION 9 — MOAT, COMPETITIVE POSITION AND INDUSTRY CONTEXT

The deep-research brief (§11 of the pack) is directionally consistent with what the company itself reports: priority brands growing 30–70% cc, generic erosion of 6pp across 2025 and 14pp in Q1-2026, margin pressure from the LOE, and a wide-moat core based on regulatory barriers, manufacturing scale, and novel modalities (radioligand, xRNA, gene therapy, and cell therapy).

**My independent assessment — what the pack's numbers show:**

1. **The moat is real and widening where it matters.** Pluvicto is growing 70% in a setting (metastatic prostate cancer) with few competing modalities; the radioligand platform is a manufacturing-and-logistics moat (radioligand supply chains are capacity-constrained and regulatorily complex). Kisqali's early-breast-cancer label is a franchise-level event (Q1-2026 sales +55% cc, $1.516B/quarter).
2. **The moat is eroding exactly where it doesn't matter anymore.** Entresto, Promacta, Tasigna are post-LOE commodities; their 40–66% declines are structural but already visible in current results and guidance.
3. **The competition is real but not unique to NVS.** The pack's brief lists Roche, AZN, LLy, MRK, PFE, ABBV, BMY. What differentiates NVS from that set: it has *already* absorbed its largest LOE in 2025–2026, while peers (MRK 2028 Keytruda LOE, ABBV 2027–2029 Humira-adjacent assets, LLy 2030 GLP-1 LOEs) carry theirs forward. From a 2027 forward-looking standpoint, NVS has the cleanest large-cap pharma patent profile.

**Data gap:** no segment revenue/margin is held in the pack (its companyfacts extract carries zero dimensional rows). I could not decompose revenue by business line from the pack; the brand-level Q1-2026 figures above come from the company release and substitute for segment detail. SOTP valuation is therefore impossible from the pack, and the DCF is the correct engine.
